# [CS012] Missing CSRF Protection (csrf-missing-protection)

A state-changing route with cookie sessions has no cross-origin protection.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-352](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/352.html) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Browsers attach cookies to requests that other sites trigger, so a form on a malicious page can submit POSTs as the victim. Go 1.25 http.CrossOriginProtection rejects cross-origin unsafe requests using Sec-Fetch-Site; gorilla/csrf, nosurf and the framework CSRF middlewares are recognized as well.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
mux.HandleFunc("POST /transfer", transfer)
http.ListenAndServe(":8080", sessions.Wrap(mux))
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
mux.HandleFunc("POST /transfer", transfer)
protect := http.NewCrossOriginProtection()
http.ListenAndServe(":8080", protect.Handler(sessions.Wrap(mux)))
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [csrf-missing-protection]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    csrf-missing-protection: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore csrf-missing-protection -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** csrf-missing-protection
```
